featured_reviews.name: Harshal Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
pure sports club without the oomph of other' clubs in South Mumbai, you shall be lucky to have a dad who bought you this memberships. Views to die for. Has a beach touch location, practically a private beach, has boating section in a Lagoon kinda water, good for amateur level water sports, club facilitates rowing, kayaking, canoeing, windsurfing, water-skiing, speed boats, probably only club in India have this facility with least entry tariff barriers. Two different swimming pools, male n females, with steam and sauna facilities of Olympic size pools hosting district n state level swimming n diving competitions. Has a Volleyball game court. Has a Badminton game court. Table Tennis room. Carrom game's, Chess board games. A Gym with two sections Air-conditioning n open air
A 100 seater dining room and another 100 seater open air dining with a sea-view, setting Sun all worthy of a lifetime.
Last and least and upgraded childrens garden to int'l style. Lil Types
About 36k members, so lil crowded so ensure you avoid weekends, else will end up with poor experience.
An Elite Club Of Members Promoted By the Erstwhile Textile Family Barons, Mafatlal Group, for only Hindu's, 90 % crowd belongs to the Gujarati, Maradwadi, Maharashtrians a typical Ghettos. Few firsts by the club, has a Olympic Sized Swimming pool and city's major competitive events are still held here. Should be only club to have a Boat Club, kinda of a private beach enterance to a lagoon kinda sea waters. Probably the only club which would have a full different pool for the females. Maintaining 2 full-sized pools just for 2 genders is high maintenance affair. Hi-tech Gym equipments. Latest Kids Garden. A decent TV room wherein 100+ plus members seat (to watch, without food being served) all sporting events live on the 100' in screen, a great family feeling. A dining room having a sunsets people could die for, not the best food, food is simply average. Has Carrom, TT, Badminton, Chess, Volleyball and a periodicals reading room.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Team  - YMCA Procter Branch Mumbai,

Today was the final day of my two-month training, and I could not let it pass without thanking the entire team.
I would like to extend my heartfelt gratitude to the entire team of YMCA Procter Branch Swimming Training Branch for providing such an excellent training experience over the last two months.

A very special thanks to Amul Raj Sir, Sebastian Paul Sir ,Peter Sir, Rashid Sir, Sadique Sir, Ashim Sir, Mr. Ali, Mr. Huzefa, and also to the Office Staff, caretakers, reception(Mr. Patil & Mr. Sudhir ) & housekeeping staff.

The entire team is truly excellent in both their work and their attitude, consistently creating a positive and motivating environment for all learners.

The program has been extremely well-structured, and I truly appreciate the dedication, support, and professionalism shown by all the coaches and staff.

Each one of them has contributed immensely—not just in teaching swimming techniques but also in creating an environment where beginners like me felt comfortable, confident, and motivated.

The trainers’ patience, personal attention, and continuous encouragement helped me overcome aquaphobia and learn to swim with confidence.

As a kidney transplant recipient who is grateful to have completed a decade post-surgery today (16th August 2025), I never imagined in my dreams that I could take up swimming. Yet, this journey has shown me that with the right guidance, patience, and encouragement, even the most distant goals can become achievable.

However, the coaches handled my case with utmost care, calmly guiding me through my skill gaps, correcting me on every dive, and advising me with patience.

While I have gained significant knowledge and comfort in swimming to the best of my physical ability, I am now motivated to further enhance my skills and continue this journey with YMCA Procter branch.

I must also mention that the pool facilities are maintained exceptionally well—clean, hygienic, and welcoming round the clock—which adds to the overall positive experience.

I would be delighted to continue my swimming journey with the YMCA Procter branch and further enhance my skills, progressing at a pace that aligns with my personal fitness and well-being.

Thank you once again to the entire YMCA Procter family for your dedication and warmth. I look forward to being part of your sessions again soon.

Warm regards,
Aamir

featured_reviews.review_text:
The history of this club is interesting, but its current policy is total nonsense. This club is strictly meant only for life members and their descendants. While I personally have no involvement with this, they should at least mention this crucial fact on their website.
​I recently moved from Sion to Tardeo, and after searching online, I visited this club today as it was the nearest swimming pool. However, the watchman informed me that membership is strictly hereditary, intended only for blood relatives. He also stated that no new memberships have been granted since 1995.
​This situation is truly disgusting because they fail to mention this restriction online. I assume that countless people must have visited over the years, only to leave disappointed. This current owner/s' mentality is extremely poor—it's a form of harassment for non-members, perhaps seeking publicity or some perverse pleasure.
​If that is not the case, they must immediately update their website with this fact. Doing so would prevent the wastage of time and harassment of non-members.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Soul-Stirring Qawwali Night with Sagar Wali Qawwali – A Modern Sufi Experience

I attended the Sagar Wali Qawwali show and it was a memorable evening of music, devotion and high-energy performance. From the moment the lights dimmed and the first note rang out, the atmosphere was charged and the audience was with the performer rather than just watching.

What stood out:
•	Sagar Bhatia’s voice and stage presence were impressive — he blends classical qawwali roots with contemporary style, making the performance feel fresh yet authentic.  ￼
•	The set-list struck a nice balance between old-school Sufi/qawwali classics and newer arrangements. According to reports, Sagar said the show sometimes “stretches because of the audience’s connection”.  ￼
•	The crowd interaction was strong — the audience sang along, clapped in unison, and the performance felt like a communal – almost spiritual – experience rather than just a concert.  ￼
•	The fusion elements (rock fusion, trumpet, modern production) lifted the show for newer listeners while keeping the Sufi core intact.  ￼

What could be improved:
•	While the modern elements are refreshing, for purists of traditional qawwali the mixing of genres and instrumentation may feel a bit “outside” the classic format. If you were expecting a completely pure dargah-style qawwali, you may notice the difference.
•	With high energy shows like this, the acoustics and sound-mix at times felt slightly over-amped/saturated (depending on venue). It may benefit from slightly more subtle sound design for certain intimate pieces.
•	On logistic side: if the venue was large (stadium or dome), the close-up connection with the performer may feel less than in a small mehfil-type setup. If you’re seated farther back, you might miss subtle expressions.

Overall verdict:
If you enjoy qawwali, Sufi music, or fusion-style live performances, this show is a strong recommendation. Sagar Wali Qawwali is not just a nostalgia act, it’s an evolution of the genre – making it accessible for younger audiences while still emotive and rooted in tradition. It delivers both on the emotional front and on the entertainment front.

Would I go again? Yes. I’ll look out for his next tour-date, maybe try a closer-venue seating for a more immersive feel.

Tip:
•	Arrive early to get a good vantage point (sound and sight).
•	Engage with the chants / clapping — the performer feeds off audience energy.
•	If possible, pick a seat closer to centre or front for more connection.
•	Bring a bit of patience if there are any small logistic delays — large live shows often have some.
•	Allow yourself to “experience”, not just “watch” — qawwali thrives on participation.

You can take the Worli sea link, which is close by, if you want to travel to the airport or other parts of Mumbai, saving you a lot of time.

Coming to the Club, i got a room in the new wing. The room was spacious (according to Mumbai standards) and had a comfortable bed, sleek LED television and well furnished with all basic amenities like AC, refrigerator etc. And the bathroom was ultra modern too, with a glass shower cubicle etc.

The only issue was, some of the rooms in the new block were being renovated (it seems because of lying closed because of lockdown). So, there were some hammering sounds etc during the day from neighbouring rooms (didn't make a difference to me, as we were out most of the day).
Not much of a view from my room, i could just see the car park, and a huge tree with hundreds of birds, but i guess their Suite room has a fabulous view of the seashore and Haji Ali (but now all broken/spoilt because of the ongoing coastal highway project construction).
Tip: I heard that the rooms in the old block  are more spacious and also tastefully done.

Coming to the food part:
There was no room service at the time of me staying because of Covid protocols.
So i really cannot comment on their service.
We went to the restaurant called Maharaj to have all our meals. And believe me, their food is Mind Blowing! Whether it was South Indian or Tandoori or the day's special Dal Pakwan, the food was EXCELLENT and at very reasonable prices. Also their service at the restaurant was exceptional.

To sum it all up, we had a memorable stay. I would give them a 5 star rating overall. Highly recommended !!

featured_reviews.review_text:
This review is only for those parent(s) who are from middle class background and who know basic swimming that was learnt from their parents or from a professional and who are expecting that their child would pick basic swimming in their 60 sessions of Michael Phelps at Sahar Plaza Andheri East.

I would not recommend this place and instead if you have a pool within your society take your kid there and teach swimming as it is not rocket science but only practice. I enrolled my six year old daughter on 05/11/2025 with expiry on July 5, 2026 for 60 sessions as you can see from the swimming card. I was told that first 12 sessions was making the kid comfortable in water, gliding in water and jumping into water without fear which my daughter did. In reality, she was doing this for 15 sessions till I took them to task and asked them when they would start teaching her swimming that only then did they began her swimming classes. My kid was happy in the pool and was picking swimming quite well with confidence till 18th March on the 28th session when the head coach asked me about renewal as there was an offer going on. I told the coach that my expiry was not due and I will do it at that time irrespective of the offer. After that on the 29th session, the instructor who was teaching my kid started behaving oddly with my kid. He would instead of focussing on her swimming, started holding her when she was swimming or when she was jumping in water. Suddenly, in that one day, my daughter told me that if she didn’t swim properly, she would drown. The next session, I again noticed the same behaviour in the instructor and I realized that the instructor was hitting the confidence of my daughter by holding her hand when she jumped in the water which was never done with her. That was the last session of my daughter with Michael Phelps and on that day I gave earful to the head coach and questioned how the instructor had undermined the confidence of my kid. I told the head coach that till date the instructor never held the hand of my daughter whenever she jumped into the water and why did he hold only her hand and not the hand of any other kids who had jumped in the water. On hindsight, I realized that since I did not commit a renewal when asked to do so, the coaches decided to slow the progress of learning swimming of my kid so that I would do another 60 sessions and what is worse is for greed of money they hit the confidence of my kid in water by instilling fear of drowning so much so that it took me another 8 sessions in the pool of my society to rectify this fear. I decided to forgo the remaining 30 sessions of my daughter as I don’t want to entrust her with teachers who instilled fear instead of positive learning and it takes a long time to unlearn that instilled fear.
Coming to my background, I learnt swimming from my mother in a local pond in 10 days and so did my husband. After that, I sharpened my swimming with breathing technique in 15 days by a trainer. All my instructors be it my mother or the trainer told me only one thing – Be free in water and water will always push you upwards and the moment you struggle you will sink, so just be free in water and feel the water. This was a positive learning that I got about swimming. This learning takes time but it is positive learning and helps in swimming. The moment you talk to a child about drowning, the child learns fear not swimming.

So for those parents who think that their kid will learn swimming here in 60 sessions, its not going to happen without a renewal at Michael Phelps. The techniques taught here are all good but when a kid’s confidence is hit, it is difficult. If you have the money, then honey Michael Phelps is for you.

featured_reviews.name: Sahaj shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am sharing this review to give honest feedback about this swimming centre.

The teachers and reception staff are generally helpful and sincere. One teacher noticed that my child was losing confidence and adjusted the training, which we really appreciated.

However, there are some areas where improvement is needed, especially since many young children attend these classes.

1. Cold Weather Conditions
Since this is an outdoor pool, strong winds blow directly onto the students during monsoon and winter. It feels cold even for parents sitting outside, and it is difficult for children after they come out of the water. When we raised this concern, we did not receive clear solutions.

2. Temperature-Regulated Pool
The pool is said to be temperature regulated, which is one reason we enrolled. However, during winter we were told that the heater was not working and would be started later. The water remained quite cold, making it difficult for children to complete their sessions comfortably.

3. Communication
Most staff members are polite, but one or two people sometimes speak in a way that feels a bit rude. A more friendly tone would help parents feel more comfortable.

4. Pool Support
There are no support rods or bars along the pool walls for children to hold. These would be helpful for beginners.

5. Washroom Facilities
Many mothers come with young children, but there is only one shower in the female washroom. Because of this, some people have to leave without washing after swimming.

Overall, the teachers are good, but some improvements in facilities and planning would make the experience much better for children and parents.
